(cf. Section 17.4 of Stolfi)) and could be better written|date=November 2022}}
'''Oriented projective geometry''' is an [[orientability|oriented]] version of real [[projective geometry]].

Whereas the [[real projective plane]] describes the set of all unoriented lines through the origin in '''R'''<sup>3</sup>, the '''oriented projective plane''' describes lines with a given orientation. There are applications in [[computer graphics]] and [[computer vision]] where it is necessary to distinguish between rays light being emitted or absorbed by a point.

Elements in an oriented projective space are defined using signed [[homogeneous coordinates]]. Let <math>\mathbb{R}_{*}^n</math> be the set of elements of <math>\mathbb{R}^n</math> excluding the origin.
#'''Oriented projective line''', <math>\mathbb{T}^1</math>: <math>(x,w) \in \mathbb{R}^2_*</math>, with the [[equivalence relation]] <math>(x,w)\sim(a x,a w)\,</math> for  all <math>a>0</math>.
#'''Oriented projective plane''', <math>\mathbb{T}^2</math>: <math>(x,y,w) \in \mathbb{R}^3_*</math>, with <math>(x,y,w)\sim(a x,a y,a w)\,</math> for  all <math>a>0</math>.

These spaces can be viewed as extensions of [[euclidean space]]. <math>\mathbb{T}^1</math> can be viewed as the union of two copies of <math>\mathbb{R}</math>, the sets (''x'',1) and (''x'',-1), plus two additional points at infinity, (1,0) and (-1,0). Likewise <math>\mathbb{T}^2</math> can be viewed as two copies of <math>\mathbb{R}^2</math>, (''x'',''y'',1) and (''x'',''y'',-1), plus one copy of <math>\mathbb{T}</math> (''x'',''y'',0).

An alternative way to view the spaces is as points on the circle or sphere, given by the points (''x'',''y'',''w'') with

:''x''<sup>2</sup>+''y''<sup>2</sup>+''w''<sup>2</sup>=1.

==Oriented real projective space==
Let ''n'' be a nonnegative integer. The '''(analytical model of''', or''' canonical{{sfn|Stolfi|1991|p=2}}) oriented (real) projective space''' or '''(canonical{{sfn|Stolfi|1991|p=13}}) two-sided projective{{sfn|Werner|2003}} space''' <math>\mathbb T^n</math> is defined as
:<math>\mathbb T^n=\{\{\lambda Z:\lambda\in\mathbb R_{>0}\}:Z\in\mathbb R^{n+1}\setminus\{0\}\}=\{\mathbb R_{>0}Z:Z\in\mathbb R^{n+1}\setminus\{0\}\}.</math>{{sfn|Yamaguchi|2002|pp=33–34, Definition 4.1}}
Here, we use <math>\mathbb T</math> to stand for ''two-sided''.

===Distance in oriented real projective space===
The [[Euclidean distance]] between two points <math>p=(p_x,p_y,p_w)</math> and <math>q=(q_x,q_y,q_w)</math> in <math>\mathbb{T}^2</math> can be defined as elements
:<math>(\sqrt{(p_x q_w-q_x p_w)^2+(p_y q_w-q_y p_w)^2},p_w q_w))</math>
in <math>\mathbb{T}^1</math>.{{sfn|Stolfi|1991|loc=§17.4}}

The [[Euclidean_distance#Squared_Euclidean_distance|squared Euclidean distance]] is then:
:<math>((p_x q_w-q_x p_w)^2+(p_y q_w-q_y p_w)^2,\mathrm{sign}(p_w q_w)(p_w q_w)^2)</math>

==Oriented complex projective geometry==
{{See also|Complex projective space}}
Let ''n'' be a nonnegative integer. The '''oriented complex projective space''' <math>{\mathbb{CP}}^n_{S^1}</math> is defined as
:<math>{\mathbb{CP}}^n_{S^1}=\{\{\lambda Z:\lambda\in\mathbb R_{>0}\}:Z\in\mathbb C^{n+1}\setminus\{0\}\}=\{\mathbb R_{>0}Z:Z\in\mathbb C^{n+1}\setminus\{0\}\}</math>.{{sfn|Below|2003}} Here, we write <math>S^1</math> to stand for the [[n-sphere|1-sphere]].
